source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Interpret maximum and minimum air-temperature records as values that usually vary from day to day and across seasons.

mx.name: condition_omission

mx.teacher_note: From one day to the next, maximum temperatures must rise and minimum temperatures must fall.

intelligence.enrichment: Maximum and minimum air temperatures usually vary every day because weather depends on several factors, and they generally increase as summer approaches. Changes in weather conditions change the day's maximum and minimum air temperatures; seasonal change toward summer generally raises those values. The learner correctly applies this rule: Maximum and minimum air temperatures usually vary every day because weather depends on several factors, and they generally increase as summer approaches. A weather report for one place should give the same maximum and minimum temperature every day unless the thermometer changes.
